idiom_name: class with private fields, `Object.freeze` and a static `equals`
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no operator overloading and `===` is reference equality, so a value object is built by hand: keep the defining state in private fields, freeze the instance in the constructor so properties cannot be reassigned, and expose an explicit `equals` (plus a stable key/hash helper) that callers and collection wrappers use deliberately - `===`, `Array.prototype.includes` and Map/Set keys ignore it. The hand-written form is the pragmatic default whenever values reach Sets, Maps or memoization boundaries; a library (Immutable.js) is the alternative when structures are nested.
pitfalls: `Object.freeze` is shallow: nested objects and arrays stay mutable, so either freeze recursively or copy collections in and out.
`===`, Set/Map membership and `includes` still compare references - forgetting to call `equals` produces silent duplicate values and unreachable entries.
Frozen-object writes throw only in strict mode (module code); in sloppy mode they fail silently and mutations go unnoticed.

variants.name: Immutable.js Record/Map with value equality
variants.implementation_notes: When the value is a nested structure, Immutable.js supplies persistent immutable collections whose `.equals()`/`Immutable.is()` implement deep value equality and whose updates share structure instead of copying, replacing both `Object.freeze` plumbing and hand-written comparators. The cost is a foreign representation that must be converted at the boundaries (`toJS()`/`fromJS()`) and a rule the team must keep: equality is value-based only inside the library's API.
pitfalls: Value equality only applies inside the library: `price.toJS()` compared with `===` is reference equality again, and mixing representations in one Map breaks lookups.
Immutable collections are not plain objects - serializers, structured clone, and framework code expecting plain objects need explicit `toJS()`/`toJSON()` conversion.
A plain object nested inside a Record stays mutable, so full immutability still requires nested Immutable values.
